# gritz

> gritz runs coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex in parallel, each in its own sandbox, driven by tasks and events.

Every page is also served as Markdown: take its URL, drop the trailing slash and append `.md`. The root page is `index.md`.

## Documentation sets

- [Complete documentation](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/llms-full.txt): every page, concatenated
- [Abridged documentation](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/llms-small.txt): every page, with non-essential content removed
- [Users](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/_llms-txt/users.txt): using gritz and its integrations
- [Operators](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/_llms-txt/operators.txt): deploying and running gritz

## Start here

- [Getting started](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/getting-started.md): Sign in to gritz, pick an organisation, create a task in the Web UI, watch it run, send a follow-up instruction and archive it.
- [What is gritz?](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/index.md): gritz runs coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex in sandboxes, driven by tasks and events.

## Concepts

- [Events and links](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/concepts/events-and-links.md): How tasks link to pull requests, issues and other resources, how a subscribed link lets an event on that resource wake the task, and where events show up.
- [Namespaces](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/concepts/namespaces.md): How a task's namespace scopes which routing rules see its subscriptions, so separate workflows on the same resource don't wake or suppress each other's tasks.
- [Organisations, members and API keys](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/concepts/orgs-members-keys.md): How organisations own tasks, runners and rules, what members and the owner can do, and what API keys and task tokens can access.
- [Routing rules](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/concepts/routing-rules.md): How an organisation's routing rules match events by type and conditions, why the first match wins, waking versus creating tasks, public rules, and testing rules with a test event.
- [Runners](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/concepts/runners.md): Where a task runs, how runners connect to an organisation, choosing a runner for a task, and what happens when a runner is offline.
- [Schedules](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/concepts/schedules.md): Create tasks on a cron schedule, in a timezone, and run a schedule's task on demand with run now.
- [Tasks](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/concepts/tasks.md): What a task is, how instructions and events start its runs, the task statuses, restarting and cancelling, archiving and auto-archive, and the task log.
- [Workspaces](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/concepts/workspaces.md): What a workspace gives a task (the image, repositories, agent and tools), how to pick one, and who defines them.

## Using gritz

- [Agent tools](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/using/agent-tools.md): The gritz tools every agent gets (get_my_task, update_my_task, create_link, report and get_github_token), what gritz tells agents to do with them, and how to write instructions that use them.
- [CLI](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/using/cli.md): Use the gritz CLI to create, list and update tasks, read a task's log, open a shell in its sandbox and get desktop notifications, and configure its server and API key.
- [Web UI](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/using/web-ui.md): A tour of the gritz Web UI, the task list and task page, schedules, events and routing rules, workspaces, members, keys and settings.

## Integrations

- [Custom events](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/integrations/custom-events.md): Send events from any system, such as an alerting tool or a deploy pipeline, to gritz so they create or wake up tasks.

## Reference

- [Custom event envelope](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/reference/custom-event-envelope.md): The request and response of POST /webhook/custom, with every field, its validation, authentication and status codes.

## Operators

- [Backends](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/operators/backends.md): The sandbox backends a runner can use, Docker and AWS Lambda MicroVMs, how each runs a task, and when to use which.
- [Debugging](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/operators/debugging.md): Read a task's driver log, log raw agent output with verbose, open a shell in a task's sandbox, and find and clean up task containers.
- [Deployment](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/operators/deployment.md): The published gritz server and runner images, running a runner as a Docker Compose service, and upgrading a deployment.
- [Operators overview](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/operators/overview.md): The parts of a gritz deployment (server, runner, driver and sandbox), who talks to whom, and what each needs to reach.
- [Runner](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/operators/runner.md): Run gritz runner on your own machine or server, with an API key, a workspaces.yaml and the driver binaries it copies into sandboxes.
- [Secrets](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/operators/secrets.md): Declare credentials in a workspace's secrets map so gritz masks them in the task log it ships to the server, and what is masked where.
- [Server](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/operators/server.md): Run gritz server with PostgreSQL, single sign-on, the GitHub App and Atlassian integrations, and the endpoints it serves.
- [workspaces.yaml](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/2063/operators/workspaces-yaml.md): Reference for the runner's workspace config, the container, setup commands, agent, MCP servers, capabilities and secrets of each workspace, and ${env:} and ${sh:} expansion.
